problem:
Consider the function $f(x)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ defined on $x\in (0,\pi ).$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(0,\frac{\pi }{2})$
- $f(x)$ is concave up on $(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi )$
- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi )$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the second derivative of $f(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x={e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ {f}^{″}(x) & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+{e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =2{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the function is concave up, we need to solve ${f}^{″}(x)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & >0 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this inequality by considering the graph of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ over the interval $(0,\pi ).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063674/assets/410e0af2ed20a065c27da5edaf0095dfd22c8a37a92e3d8fbaeece629cefa278.png)

From the graph, we see that $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0$ when $0<x<\frac{\pi }{2}.$ So the graph is concave up on the interval $(0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$

The function $f(x)$ is concave down when ${f}^{″}(x)<0.$ By similar reasoning to before, this leads to the inequality $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ which has the solution $(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
